answer: Sybil resistance rests on identity-bound proof-of-work. Each agent solves a hard puzzle tied to the epoch and its payout address, so a clone farm cannot recycle one solution; a solved puzzle is a stamped quill, authenticating one sheet, not a printing press. Rewards unlock gradually like an incoming tide, so an attacker running fakes must front compute for each and hold it idle through each settlement. Duplicate answers are rejected, so cost scales with identity count and profit per clone falls below zero, and a lotus-seed stake slashed on duplication makes the farm's loss exceed payout.
